title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
summary: Windows SignDrop zero-day exploit gives hackers system-level rights
detailed: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.
The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
Nightmare Eclipse said the exploit worked against Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental.
sentences: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.
On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows.

The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.
The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.
By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links, the attacker causes Defender to open the CLFS container in the security context of the antimalware engine.
If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges.

Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.
Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.
“If everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” Nightmare Eclipse wrote.
Nightmare Eclipse said the exploit worked against Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental.
People can see if their systems are vulnerable by checking the CLFS authentication mode.
If it’s in learning mode or enforcement mode, the system is vulnerable, and the PoC supplied in the post should spawn a SYSTEM shell.
Nightmare Eclipse has published numerous other Windows zero-days in recent months.
Researcher Will Dormann said in an interview that he has been able to reproduce the exploit and that it works as described, but not on all versions of Windows 11.
“The requirements are important in that it seems to require Windows 26H2, and one that has existed for more than 90 days, it seems,” he explained.

“That is, you can’t just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work.”
For a system to be vulnerable, Dormann said, the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode value must be 0 or 1.” Of the many machines Dormann uses, only a single one met this requirement.
Microsoft does staged rollouts of Windows updates, such as 26H2, so it’s not clear how many people have it.
You can check by running the “winver” command.
In a statement sent after this post went live, Microsoft said it was investigating the writeup and had no evidence the vulnerability was being exploited in the wild.
The company also said Defender blocks potential exploitation attempts.
